fixtures.source: WXF2018 1.4 and 2.1–2.7; independently reviewed MSH80 XQ-F001
fixtures.reasoning: Setup-derived exhaustive list: 4 rook + 4 horse + 4 elephant + 2 advisor + 1 general + 24 cannon + 5 soldier = 44. No perft or comparator output used.
Open rook has eight horizontal and nine vertical destinations, except own General e0; e0 is excluded by friendly occupancy.
Friendly c4 stops left ray before c4; enemy e6 is capturable and stops the upward ray; own General stops downward ray.
Boundary rook has only positive file/rank rays; e0 is occupied by its General and blocks the rank.
Without a screen a cannon moves quietly along open rook rays; the General e0 blocks its downward ray.
A cannon cannot capture with zero screens, cannot jump an enemy as a quiet move, and may stop before it.
One friendly screen enables capture of nearest enemy e8; empty e7 beyond the screen is not a quiet destination.
One enemy screen enables capture of nearest enemy e8; the mount itself cannot be captured by this cannon.
Two screens prevent the e9 capture. Friendly second screen cannot be captured; no landing past first screen without an enemy capture.
Nearest enemy beyond one screen is e7; e9 has two intervening pieces and cannot be captured.
All four horse legs are empty, giving exactly eight two-by-one destinations.
Friendly e5 blocks the north leg and both d6/f6 destinations only.
Enemy f4 blocks the east leg and both g3/g5 destinations only; the horse cannot capture its leg blocker.
Boundary horse has two in-board moves and six off-board candidates.
Home Elephant moves two diagonals through b1/d1; both eyes are empty.
Friendly b1 blocks the a2 eye but not e2.
Enemy d1 blocks the e2 eye just as a friendly eye blocker would.
Interior home-side Elephant has all four eye-clear diagonal moves.
At rank4 the two increasing-rank Elephant moves cross the river and are forbidden.
Advisor in palace corner d0 has one legal diagonal destination e1.
Central palace Advisor has exactly four diagonal palace destinations; no orthogonal move.
Upper palace corner Advisor cannot leave its palace on diagonals to g1/g3/e3.
General in d0 palace corner may move one orthogonal step; neither destination faces the opposing General.
General f1 destination is inside its palace but faces f9 and is forbidden; other three orthogonal steps are safe.
Uncrossed edge Soldier can only advance; sideways and backward are forbidden.
A Soldier on rank4 has not yet crossed the river; crossing occurs by its forward move to rank5.
A Soldier on rank5 has crossed the river, gains sideways movement, and still cannot retreat.
Post-river edge Soldier has one forward and one inward lateral move; no off-board or backward action.

At the far rank, Soldier cannot advance or retreat. It may move laterally to d9; f9 is the opposing General and is never a capturable piece (2.8). This root already threatens f9, so it is a structural-only rejection diagnostic.
The horse is the sole facing-General blocker. Every horse departure exposes the Generals, hence its entire legal action set is empty.
General d0-e0 would newly face e9 without an intervening piece and is forbidden.
Even capturing the enemy horse on f6 does not excuse exposing the Generals by vacating the e-file.
Pinned rook must remain on the e-file or capture the checking-line rook; horizontal departures expose its General.
Moving f1 rook off the enemy horse leg exposes the General; capturing the horse is a valid cure.
Two existing cannon screens are safe; moving one off the e-file creates exactly one screen and exposes check.
Rook line check can only be escaped here by d0 or f0; e1 remains attacked.
Capture e1 removes the checker. d0 is safe. f0 faces the opposing General f9 and is forbidden.
Only rook a1-e1 blocks the e-file check; General d0 escapes; f0 faces f9.

Horse f2 checks e0 through f1; rook a1-f1 blocks that leg. General d0/e1/f0 all escape: on f0, the horse f2 itself interposes between the Generals, and a horse on f2 does not attack f0. Thus there are exactly four evasions.
Friendly rook is the single cannon mount: moving it off-file or capturing the cannon cures check; leaving it on-file does not.
Adding a second screen by a2-e2 cures cannon check; an unrelated rook move does not.
Capturing the enemy mount a4-e4 merely replaces it with the friendly rook: one screen remains and check is not cured.
General is not presently checked, but d0/f0 are attacked by the respective rooks and e1 by both. This proves zero local actions without assigning a game result.
Rook d0 checks; capturing it exposes the horse c2 attack on d0. The f0/e1 escapes are covered by f1 rook. Zero local actions is distinct from the prior non-check case.
The rook has an unobstructed line capture of enemy Rook. The captured family has no hand/promotion effect.
The rook has an unobstructed line capture of enemy Cannon. The captured family has no hand/promotion effect.
The rook has an unobstructed line capture of enemy Horse. The captured family has no hand/promotion effect.
The rook has an unobstructed line capture of enemy Soldier. The captured family has no hand/promotion effect.
The rook has an unobstructed line capture of enemy Elephant. The captured family has no hand/promotion effect.
The rook has an unobstructed line capture of enemy Advisor. The captured family has no hand/promotion effect.
General capture is explicitly excluded even on a structural diagram already checking the opposing General. No king-capture continuation is admitted.
